'''Lars Chittka''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]], [[Fellow of the Linnean Society|FLS]], [[Royal Entomological Society|FRES]], [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Biology|FRSB]] (born April 1963) is a German [[zoologist]], [[ethologist]] and [[ecologist]] distinguished for his work on the [[evolution]] of [[sensory system]]s and [[cognition]], using insect-flower interactions as a model.

== Life and career ==
Born in [[Germany]], Chittka studied [[Biology]] at the [[Georg-August-Universität Göttingen]] and the [[Free University of Berlin]].<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Chittka |first1=Lars |title=Lars Chittka |journal=Current Biology |date=December 2010 |volume=20 |issue=23 |pages=R1006–R1008 |doi=10.1016/j.cub.2010.09.062 |bibcode=2010CBio...20R1006C |s2cid=1275714 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://news.mongabay.com/2010/06/uncovering-the-intelligence-of-insects-an-interview-with-lars-chittka/|title=Uncovering the intelligence of insects, an interview with Lars Chittka|website=news.mongabay.com|access-date=2016-11-17|date=2010-06-29}}</ref> He obtained his PhD degree under the supervision of Randolf Menzel at the [[Free University of Berlin]]. Chittka is a recipient of the [[Royal Society]] Wolfson Research Merit Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2014/wolfson-merit-awards-may/|title=Royal Society announces new round of esteemed Wolfson Research Merit Awards|website=royalsociety.org|access-date=2016-11-17}}</ref> and an Advanced Fellowship from the [[European Research Council]] (ERC).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://erc.europa.eu/space-use-bees%E2%80%93-radar-tracking-spatial-movement-patterns-key-pollinators|title=Space use by bees– radar tracking of spatial movement patterns of key pollinators {{!}} ERC: European Research Council|website=erc.europa.eu|access-date=2016-11-17}}</ref> He is also member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]], an elected Fellow of the [[Linnean Society of London|Linnean Society]] (FLS), the [[Royal Entomological Society]] (FRES) as well as the [[Royal Society of Biology]] (FRSB).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://chittkalab.sbcs.qmul.ac.uk/Lars.html|title=Chittka Lab – Lars Chittka|last=Chittka|first=Lars|website=chittkalab.sbcs.qmul.ac.uk|access-date=2016-11-17}}</ref> He received the Lesley Goodman Award of the Royal Entomological Society in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.royensoc.co.uk/awards/RES_Goodman_award.htm|title=RES Goodman Award {{!}} Royal Entomological Society|last=Society|first=Royal Entomological|date=2010-12-06|website=www.royensoc.co.uk|access-date=2016-11-17}}</ref> Lars Chittka has been an Editor of Biology's foremost open access journal [[PLOS Biology|PLoS Biology]] since 2004,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/s/editorial-board|title=PLOS Biology: A Peer-Reviewed Open-Access Journal|website=journals.plos.org|access-date=2016-11-17}}</ref> and has also been on the Editorial Board of [[Proceedings of the Royal Society of London]] Series B (2010–2012) and the [[The Quarterly Review of Biology|Quarterly Review of Biology]] (2004–2010);<ref name=":2" /> he is a member of the [[Faculty of 1000]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://f1000.com/prime/thefaculty/member/8351263021504972|title=F1000 members|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=}}</ref> (now known as Faculty Opinions) and was a Panel Chairman for the European Research Council (2010–2013).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/ERC_2011_StG_Panel_Members.pdf|title=ERC 2011 panel members|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=}}</ref> He is also the founder of the Research Centre for Psychology at [[Queen Mary University of London]],<ref name=":0" /> where he is a Professor of Sensory and Behavioural Ecology.<ref name=":2" /> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-27|title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2026/05/new-fellows-announcement-2026/|access-date=2026-05-31|website=Royal Society|language=en}}</ref>

== Research achievements ==
Chittka has carried out extensive work on the behaviour, cognition and ecology of [[bumblebee]]s and [[Honey bee|honeybees]], and their interactions with flowers.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> He developed perceptual models of animal colour vision, allowing the derivation of optimal receiver systems as well as a quantification of the evolutionary pressures shaping flower signals. Chittka also made fundamental contributions to the understanding of [[animal cognition]] and its fitness benefits in the economy of nature. He explored phenomena such as numerosity, speed-accuracy trade-offs, false memories and [[Social learning in animals|social learning]] in bees.<ref name=":2" /> His discoveries have made a substantial impact on the understanding of animal intelligence and its neural-computational underpinnings. He has published over 250 peer-reviewed articles,<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":4">{{Google scholar id|ux2CNs0AAAAJ}}</ref> many of them highly cited.<ref name=":4" />

== Science, music and art ==
Chittka has been involved in a number of collaborative works linking the science of bees with music and art. With musicians Katie Green and Rob Alexander, he formed the band Killer Bee Queens.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/video/sex-death-rock-n-roll-152856137.html|title = Sex, death, rock 'n' roll: The life of a bee| date=31 October 2019 }}</ref> In 2019, they released the [[post-punk]] inspired concept album Strange Flowers on [[Bandcamp]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://killerbeequeens.bandcamp.com/releases|title=Strange Flowers, by Killer Bee Queens}}</ref> Two music videos were published; "I stung Gwyneth Paltrow" <ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211209/fgVZrnGDNKA Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20200306071901/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fgVZrnGDNKA Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite AV media| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fgVZrnGDNKA| title = Killer Bee Queens 'I Stung Gwyneth Paltrow' (Official Video) | website=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref> referred to the pseudoscientific method of bee stings as a treatment for minor skin conditions, as advocated by the actress.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vogue.com/article/gwyneth-paltrow-apitherapy-bee-stings-treatment|title = Inside Gwyneth Paltrow's Latest Wellness Adventure: Bee Sting Therapy|date = 6 April 2016}}</ref> The video for "The Beekeeper's Dream" used footage from [[David Blair (filmmaker)|David Blair]]'s  1991 surrealist film "[[Wax or the Discovery of Television Among the Bees]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vimeo.com/484469995|title=Killer Bee Queens – the Beekeeper's Dream (Subtitles)}}</ref>

Chittka also worked with installation artist Julian Walker on a project in which live bees' responses to famous paintings were evaluated ("Do Bees Like Van Gogh's Sunflowers?").<ref name="Chittka & Walker 2006">{{cite journal |last1=Chittka |first1=Lars |last2=Walker |first2=Julian |title=Do bees like Van Gogh's Sunflowers? |journal=Optics & Laser Technology |date=June 2006 |volume=38 |issue=4–6 |pages=323–328 |doi=10.1016/j.optlastec.2005.06.020 |bibcode=2006OptLT..38..323C }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Science |first1=American Association for the Advancement of |title=Bees for Van Gogh |journal=Science |date=26 August 2005 |volume=309 |issue=5739 |page=1322 |doi=10.1126/science.309.5739.1322a |s2cid=172363973 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/4150200.stm|title = Art-loving bees prefer Sunflowers|date = 14 August 2005}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.artlink.com.au/articles/3722/insects-as-art-lovers-bees-for-van-gogh/|title=Insects as art lovers: Bees for van Gogh}}</ref> Chittka and Walker explained that they used "this unconventional approach in the hope to raise awareness for between-species differences in visual perception, and to provoke thinking about the implications of biology in human aesthetics and the relationship between object representation and its biological connotations."<ref name="Chittka & Walker 2006"/>

Data collected by Chittka's team on the life-long radar-tracking of individual bumblebees' flights<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Woodgate |first1=Joseph L. |last2=Makinson |first2=James C. |last3=Lim |first3=Ka S. |last4=Reynolds |first4=Andrew M. |last5=Chittka |first5=Lars |title=Life-Long Radar Tracking of Bumblebees |journal=PLOS ONE |date=4 August 2016 |volume=11 |issue=8 |article-number=e0160333 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0160333 |pmid=27490662 |pmc=4973990 |bibcode=2016PLoSO..1160333W |doi-access=free }}</ref> formed the basis for artwork by [[Lucy Pullen]] which was on display at the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] from 2018-2020. Some of the images are now in a collection of the Royal Bank of Canada, Toronto.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lucypullen.com/bees/27gp0zs0do8ysakskh5wmtac3ydglb|title = Bees}}</ref>

Chittka also contributed to a science-music project with artist Aladin Borioli, called "Shared Sensibilities"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.apian.ch/news/apian-on-bbc-radio-6-music/|title = Home – Apian – A machine for exploring the age-old interspecies relationship between bees and humans| date=13 October 2023 }}</ref> in which sections of an interview about Chittka's research were combined with the music of Laurent Güdel<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://laurentgudel.tumblr.com/biography|title = Biography}}</ref> and the sounds of honeybees, aired on BBC Radio 6 in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m000q44p|title = BBC Radio 6 Music – BBC Introducing Arts with Gemma Cairney, 07/12/2020}}</ref>
